title: AWS service map (compute, storage, networking, security)
hook: AWS offers hundreds of services. Interviews do not expect you to memorize every name — they expect you to map a problem to the right category and pick the flagship service in each.

blocks.text: The AWS service map groups offerings by job: compute (EC2, Lambda, Elastic Container Service (ECS)), storage (S3, Elastic Block Store (EBS), Elastic File System (EFS)), networking (Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), Route 53, CloudFront), databases (RDS, DynamoDB), security (IAM, Key Management Service (KMS), Web Application Firewall (WAF)), and integration (Simple Queue Service (SQS), Simple Notification Service (SNS), EventBridge). Knowing the map lets you answer 'where would you put X?' without listing every product.

entries.plainDefinition: Virtual servers you control — classic Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).
entries.example: A .NET API on Windows or Linux VMs.

entries.plainDefinition: Object storage for files, backups, and static assets.
Your isolated network inside AWS with subnets, routes, and gateways.
entries.example: 10.0.0.0/16 private network for all app tiers.

entries.plainDefinition: Users, roles, and policies that control who can call which AWS API.
entries.example: Lambda execution role with read-only S3 access.

blocks.text: Senior interviews test pattern recognition: static site → S3 + CloudFront; background job → SQS + Lambda; relational data → RDS or Aurora; high-scale key-value → DynamoDB. Naming the wrong category (putting a queue in S3) signals shallow AWS exposure.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Start with category, then one flagship service, then mention alternatives only if asked.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Edge and DNS
items.body: Route 53 resolves domain; CloudFront caches static assets.

items.title: Compute
items.body: Application Load Balancer (ALB) routes to ECS tasks or EC2 instances.

items.title: Data
items.body: RDS for relational state; Redis (ElastiCache) for session cache.

items.title: Async
items.body: SQS decouples write path; Lambda or workers process messages.

snippet.label: CLI: discover services in your account
snippet.code:
aws service-quotas list-services --query 'Services[?ServiceName==`Amazon Simple Storage Service` || ServiceName==`Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud`].ServiceCode' --output table

aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources \
  --tag-filters Key=Application,Values=orders-api \
  --resource-type-filters ec2:instance s3:bucket rds:db
snippet.explanation: list-services maps human names to quota codes. Resource Groups Tagging API finds resources across service categories by tag.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: mini three-tier stack
snippet.code:
Resources:
  AppVpc:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
    Properties:
      CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
  AppBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  AppQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: orders-events
snippet.explanation: One template spans networking (VPC), storage (S3), and messaging (SQS) — the core categories most architectures combine.

snippet.label: CLI: list enabled Regions for a service
snippet.code:
aws ec2 describe-regions --region-names us-east-1 eu-west-1 ap-south-1 --output table

aws s3api list-buckets --query 'Buckets[].Name'
snippet.explanation: Not every service is in every Region. Always verify Regional availability before designing multi-Region.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using EC2 for every problem when Lambda or Fargate fits. Storing relational data in S3 instead of RDS/DynamoDB. Forgetting IAM and VPC touch every category — they are not optional add-ons.

interviewTakeaways: Group AWS services by job: compute, storage, networking, database, security, integration.
Start answers with category + flagship service; add alternatives only when probed.
Tag resources with Application and Environment so cross-service inventory stays searchable.
60s: Web API: Route 53, CloudFront, ALB, ECS/EC2, RDS, S3, SQS, IAM, VPC. Pick compute by operational model — VM, container, or function.
Follow-up: when would you choose DynamoDB over RDS?
commonPitfalls: Listing 20 service names without a category — interviewers want structured thinking, not memorization.
Strong answer: name the problem, map to category, pick default service, mention one tradeoff.
Putting message queues in S3 or using Lambda for 15-minute CPU-bound batch without considering Fargate.
Ignoring Regional service availability when designing global architecture.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Express on EC2 is IaaS. Express on Elastic Beanstalk is PaaS-style. API Gateway + Lambda is function-as-a-service. Same TypeScript code can map to different AWS compute categories.
